L8: # AFT, UFT and Microsoft announce ‘National AI Safety & Privacy Standard’ for schools to protect students, families and educators
L9: ## Landmark agreement hands parents and educators control through legally enforceable guardrails, builds on NYC schools’ screen and AI ban
L10: 
L11:   * cite4†Microsoft Source L12: NEW YORK — Sept. 9, 2026 — After months of intense negotiations and in the absence of any meaningful federal and state rules governing artificial intelligence in schools, AFT President Randi Weingarten, United Federation of Teachers President Michael Mulgrew, and Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith today announced a “cite5†National AI Safety & Privacy Standard†cdn-dynmedia-1.microsoft.com ” establishing legally enforceable protections to ensure the safety of students, families and educators.
L13: The first-of-its-kind cite6†agreement†www.aft.org on the heels of New York City Public Schools’ screens and AI ban, ensures that tech companies cannot use student data to train AI, students can never be tracked, AI cannot make decisions without human oversight, and companies must give educators and parents transparency and plain-language answers about how their tools work. U.S.
L14: school districts can incorporate these protections directly into their Microsoft customer agreements, making them contractually enforceable.
L15: “We have forged a hard-fought, iron-clad privacy agreement with real teeth that protects students and families, because no one else, including the federal government, has stepped up to do the real work,” Weingarten said. “We can get angrier and angrier, or we can act decisively; anything less than legally enforceable provisions is simply a wish list.”
L16: Weingarten continued, “This agreement ensures three foundational goals: protect the privacy and data of children, give schools real control over AI tools in the classroom, and provide transparency and information to parents. And with New York City adopting our framework to ban screens and AI use in the younger years, this agreement adds to the momentum around online safety for kids and educators.”
L17: In a May speech, “cite7†Devices Down, Eyes Up, Hands-On†www.aft.org ,” Weingarten flagged her fight for an enforceable data privacy standard and called for a total screen ban from kindergarten through second grade, a ban on student-facing AI in elementary school and a ban on social companion chat bots for students under 16.
L18: A similar framework has been adopted by the Los Angeles Unified School District, the New York State United Teachers (the AFT’s state affiliate), and last week, New York City Public Schools and Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
L19: “This standard sets a high bar for child privacy and AI safety, and we’ll extend this agreement to every school district across the country,” said Microsoft’s Smith.
L20: 
L21: At its core, the agreement turns shared principles into clear, enforceable protections centered on three priorities:
L22:   * Protecting privacy: Educators, parents and students can have confidence that data remains theirs. Student and educator data will not be used to train AI models, sold or repurposed, and schools will maintain control over how data is used, retained and deleted.
L23:   * Enhancing safety: Students and educators are protected by strong security, safeguards and human oversight. AI systems must be designed to avoid harmful or manipulative experiences, protect sensitive information, and meet rigorous standards for security, accountability and responsible use.
L24:   * Providing transparency and control: Families can expect clear, accessible information about how AI is being used in schools and their safeguards, including what data is collected and what protections are in place. Schools retain control over when and how AI is used, and companies need to communicate clearly about product changes, risks and controls.
L25: “Educators are stepping in to do what we do best: protect our students. This agreement gives families and school districts the information and privacy protections they have been demanding, and it empowers school districts to end agreements and seek damages from bad actors who break the rules.
L26: It starts to level the playing field in a competitive, ever-changing arena that lacks the guardrails our children and school communities need,” said the UFT’s Mulgrew, who leads the 200,000-member New York City AFT affiliate.
L27: In 2024, the AFT released its “cite8†Commonsense Guardrails for Using Advanced Technology in Schools†www.aft.org ,” which established nine core principles to ensure students and families were informed and protected. And last year, it announced the creation of the cite9†National Academy for AI Instruction†www.aft.org , which enables educators to access training on the use and misuse of AI tools rather than being treated like an afterthought, as so often happens with changes in education technology.
L28: Led by educators, the academy allows teachers not only to become proficient with the emerging technology but to be diligent about student safety and privacy.
L29: “HIPAA and FERPA never envisioned the advent of AI,” Weingarten said, “and in the absence of those protections, tech companies need to take responsibility for the products they create and market to students, educators and communities.”
L30: 
L31: A fact sheet on the agreement can be viewed cite10†here†aka.ms , and the full agreement can be viewed cite6†here†www.aft.org .
L32: Microsoft (Nasdaq “MSFT” @microsoft) creates platforms and tools powered by AI to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The technology company is committed to making AI available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

L2@P0: Preamble — Why This Agreement Exists
L3@P0: This Memorandum of Agreement exists for one reason: children come first.
L4@P0: Students are not products. Teachers are not beta testers. And schools are not a source for data
L5@P0: collection or experiments. When artificial intelligence tools enter a classroom, they bring
L6@P0: enormous potential, and equally enormous responsibility. This agreement sets one of the
L7@P0: highest standards for how that responsibility must be met.
L8@P0: Likewise, the National Academy for AI Instruction is not a data company. The Academy is a
L9@P0: national initiative dedicated to equipping educators with the knowledge, skills, and support to
L10@P0: use artificial intelligence effectively and responsibly in teaching and learning.
L11@P0: This is a binding Memorandum of Agreement between the National Academy for AI Instruction
L12@P0: (referred to throughout as "the Academy") and any AI Provider that the Academy engages to
L13@P0: provide AI-powered services to educators or students. Every requirement in this agreement is
L14@P0: mandatory. Vendors who cannot meet these requirements are not eligible to serve the Academy
L15@P0: or to achieve the Standard. The Standard is a seal of excellence and a public commitment to
L16@P0: the safety, privacy, and well-being of children, families, and educators. It signifies that an AI
L17@P0: Provider has met the Academy’s highest standards for responsible, trustworthy, and educationcentered artificial intelligence.
L18@P0: Memorandum guiding principle: When in doubt, protect the students, families, and educators.
L19@P0: Beyond the Academy
L20@P0: The signatories to this Standard agree that the principles set out below do not belong only to the
L21@P0: Academy but are available to any school district that desires the same principles to apply when
L22@P0: purchasing AI Provider Educational Products. Each AI Provider that signs this agreement will
L23@P0: create a clear, simple, and expeditious process through which any school district can request
L24@P0: that the Provider meet or exceed the Standard in its own specific agreements for the AI Provider
L25@P0: Educational Products (defined below). As a best practice, each AI Provider will encourage
L26@P0: AI SAFETY & PRIVACY
L27@P0: STANDARD FOR SCHOOLS
L28@P0: MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT
L29@P0: To Protect Students, Families and Educators
L30@P0: Highest Level of Protection | Ten Principles | Fully Enforceable
L31@P0-1: September 2026, Version 1.0NATIONAL AI SAFETY & PRIVACY STANDARD MOA | National Academy for AI Instruction September 2026
L32@P1: When in doubt, protect the student. Page 2 of 31
L33@P1: school districts to adopt the Standard and will support districts seeking to incorporate its
L34@P1: principles into their agreements. Each participating AI Provider will make the substantive
L35@P1: protections of the Standard available to EDU Customers upon request within 90 days of the
L36@P1: Effective Date, provided that such protections may be incorporated into the EDU Customer’s
L37@P1: existing data privacy agreement, licensing agreement, or addendum and need not be adopted in
L38@P1: the identical form set forth in the Standard. The process should be easy to find and easy to use,
L39@P1: and a district can make the request at any time. Once a district makes the request, the AI
L40@P1: Provider will work diligently to incorporate the applicable terms into that district’s agreement.
L41@P1: Key Definitions
L42@P1: As used in this Standard:
L43@P1: • "Student Data" means any information that is directly related to an identifiable student,
L44@P1: including but not limited to: names, student ID numbers, grades, disciplinary records,
L45@P1: prompts entered into AI Provider Educational Product, AI-generated outputs tied to a
L46@P1: student, behavioral patterns, device identifiers, location data, memory files, audio or
L47@P1: visual data, and metadata. This definition is intentionally broad. When in doubt about
L48@P1: whether something is Student Data, treat it as Student Data.
L49@P1: • "Covered Data" means Student Data plus any data belonging to or generated by
L50@P1: educators, administrators, or an EDU Customer (including the Academy) when using AI
L51@P1: Provider Educational Products. Covered Data does not include Telemetry Data (as
L52@P1: defined below).
L53@P1: • “Telemetry Data” means technical and operational data generated through the use or
L54@P1: operation of the AI Provider Educational Products that has been de-identified so that it
L55@P1: cannot reasonably be used to identify, relate to, describe, or be linked to an individual
L56@P1: student, or educator. Telemetry Data may be associated with an EDU Customer solely
L57@P1: for security, reliability, debugging, capacity planning, service health, aggregate
L58@P1: performance monitoring, and to make product improvements. Telemetry Data may not
L59@P1: be used, directly or indirectly, for generative-model training, student profiling, individual
L60@P1: student user personalization of AI outputs, advertising, marketing, behavioral inference,
L61@P1: or the creation or enhancement of profiles concerning individual users.
L62@P1: • "AI Provider" means the company providing the AI-powered service, including all
L63@P1: subsidiaries, affiliates, contractors, and sub processors.
L64@P1: • "Training" means any use of data to develop, fine-tune, update, improve, or otherwise
L65@P1: alter an AI model's weights, parameters, or behaviors.
L66@P1: • “AI Provider Educational Products” means services or features that use generative
L67@P1: artificial intelligence technologies to generate outputs that are primarily designed and
L68@P1: marketed for use by students, educators and administrators, with authenticated usage
L69@P1: under an agreement between the educational entity and the AI Provider. For the
L70@P1: avoidance of doubt, general-purpose productivity, collaboration, communication, search,
L71@P1: cloud, development, or workplace-assistance products, including products that may be
L72@P1: licensed or used by educational entities but are not primarily designed for educational
L73@P1: purposes do not constitute an AI Provider Educational Product.
L74@P1: • “EDU Customer” means an educational entity located in the United States that licenses
L75@P1: AI Provider Educational Products from AI Provider. For clarity, the Academy may be an
L76@P1-2: EDU Customer when it licenses such AI Provider Educational Products.NATIONAL AI SAFETY & PRIVACY STANDARD MOA | National Academy for AI Instruction September 2026
L77@P2: When in doubt, protect the student. Page 3 of 31
L78@P2: PRINCIPLE 1 | No Student or Educator Data for Training — Ever, With
L79@P2: One Narrow Safety Exception
L80@P2: • "Academy" means the signing institution, including its students, educators, staff, and
L81@P2: administrators.
L82@P2: • "Breach" means any unauthorized access to, disclosure of, alteration of, or destruction
L83@P2: of Covered Data.
L84@P2: • "Zero Data Retention (ZDR)" means that inputs (prompts) and outputs (responses) are
L85@P2: not stored, logged, or retained beyond the immediate session required to deliver the
L86@P2: service.
L87@P2: • "Synthetic Data" means data that is artificially generated to simulate patterns, scenarios,
L88@P2: or edge cases. Under this agreement, Synthetic Data may be used only if it is not
L89@P2: created from, seeded with, tuned on, or reasonably reversible to Covered Data.
L90@P2: • "Agentic or Action-Taking Feature" means any AI capability that can initiate, approve,
L91@P2: transmit, modify, or execute actions on behalf of a user, online or offline, rather than only
L92@P2: generating informational output.
L93@P2: • "Memory Files" means anything an AI Provider Educational Product saves about a user
L94@P2: between sessions, stored facts, preferences, profiles, or conversation summaries, so it
L95@P2: can "remember" them later. All Memory Files are Covered Data under this agreement.
L96@P2: PART I — THE TEN CORE PRINCIPLES
L97@P2: Each principle below is a binding commitment. The AI Provider must comply with all ten, across
L98@P2: every AI Provider Educational Product it provides to an EDU Customer who has opted in to the
L99@P2: principles. Complying with some principles but not others is not compliance.
L100@P2: These principles are effective from the date signed and remain in force for a term of two years
L101@P2: (the “Effective Date”). To continue past that term, the agreement must be renewed in writing by
L102@P2: both the Academy and the AI Provider every two years. The Academy may terminate the AI
L103@P2: Provider's participation in the Standard immediately upon any material breach by the AI
L104@P2: Provider that is not cured within the period set forth in Principle 5.
L105@P2: Compliance with Applicable Laws
L106@P2: All aspects of this Standard shall be implemented in accordance with all applicable federal,
L107@P2: state, and local laws and regulations, including FERPA, COPPA, IDEA, and applicable student
L108@P2: privacy, data protection, accessibility, civil rights, consumer protection, and education laws.
L109@P2: Nothing in this Standard limits any right, protection, or obligation provided by law. Where this
L110@P2: Standard provides stronger protections, those stronger protections shall apply to the extent
L111@P2: permitted by law.
L112@P2: The AI Provider absolutely may not use any Covered Data, including prompts, responses,
L113@P2: uploaded files, behavioral signals, metadata, or any derivative thereof, to train, fine-tune,
L114@P2: update, benchmark, or otherwise improve any AI model, at any time, for any purpose, except as
L115@P2-3: expressly permitted under the Narrow Safety and Security Exception below.NATIONAL AI SAFETY & PRIVACY STANDARD MOA | National Academy for AI Instruction September 2026
L116@P3: When in doubt, protect the student. Page 4 of 31
L117@P3: This prohibition:
L118@P3: • Applies to all data types without exception: text, audio, images, video, biometrics,
L119@P3: metadata, interaction logs.
L120@P3: • Applies to de-identified, aggregated, transformed, or other Covered-Data-derived
L121@P3: datasets. De-identification is not a loophole, and Covered Data may not be used as
L122@P3: source material for synthetic data generation.

L134@P3: Narrow Safety and Security Exception
L135@P3: Covered Data may be used for safety and security purposes only under all the following
L136@P3: conditions:
L137@P3: • Safety and Security Functionality. The exception applies only to processing that is
L138@P3: reasonably necessary to detect, prevent, investigate, mitigate, or remediate harm to
L139@P3: users or threats to the security or integrity of the AI Provider Educational Products,
L140@P3: including self-harm risk, child sexual abuse material, grooming, threats of violence,
L141@P3: bullying, malicious activity, security incidents, vulnerabilities, or unauthorized access.
L142@P3: Safety or security functionality may be technically integrated into a broader model,
L143@P3: system, or product that performs other functions, provided that the processing of
L144@P3: Covered Data under this exception remains strictly limited to the safety or security
L145@P3: purposes described in this paragraph.
L146@P3: • Purpose-Limited Use. Covered Data processed under this exception may be used
L147@P3: solely for the applicable safety or security purpose and may not be used for general
L148@P3: model training or improvement, user profiling, personalization, advertising, behavioral
L149@P3: inference, market research, development of unrelated products or functionality, or other
L150@P3: commercial purposes.
L151@P3: • Minimum Necessary. The AI Provider may process only the minimum amount of
L152@P3: Covered Data reasonably necessary to accomplish the applicable safety or security
L153@P3: purpose and must use reasonably available technical and organizational measures to
L154@P3: minimize the Covered Data processed.
L155@P3: • Retention Limits. Covered Data processed under this exception may be retained only
